chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya narrated from Ibrahim ibn Hashim, from Dawud ibn Muhammad al-Nahdi, from some of our companions, who said:

Ibn Abi Sa'id al-Mukari entered upon al-Rida (peace be upon him) and said to him, 'I ask you about a matter.' He said, 'I do not think you will accept from me, and you are not from my flock, but bring it forth.'
A man said, 'He said, 'At my death, every slave of mine who is 'qadeem' (old/long-held) is free for the sake of Allah.'
He (al-Rida) said, 'Yes, for Allah says in His Book,
until it becomes like an old, crooked root
Then, any of his slaves who has been with him for six months is considered 'qadeem' and thus free.'
ai.seo_question: What is the duration required for a slave to be considered 'qadeem' for manumission according to Imam al-Rida?
ai.summary: Imam al-Rida (AS) provides a precise juristic definition of 'qadeem' (old/long-held) for the purpose of manumission, ruling that a slave attains this status after six months of ownership. He grounds this legal deduction in the Quranic usage of the term 'qadeem' to denote age or antiquity, illustrating the Shia method of deriving specific fiqh rulings from general Quranic terminology.
